The **Danish Clinical Register of Emergency Surgery** is a former national database in Denmark that served as the direct predecessor to the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] [^src1]. It played a foundational role in the country's emergency surgery research, providing the underlying data for several scientific studies that are cited in the methodological background of the 2024 annual report [^src1]. 

According to the scientific reference list and methodological framework detailed on pages 86–90 of the report, the current Akut Kirurgi Databasen builds directly upon earlier register research, most notably the Danish Clinical Register of Emergency Surgery and the PULP trial [^src1]. This historical data was instrumental in developing the 11 evidence-based clinical quality indicators currently in use, which are tied to specific treatment goals and deadlines [^src1]. The transition from this older register to the newer platform reflects ongoing efforts to manage practical challenges regarding data quality and hospital-level registration practices [^src1].
